judgment.rationale: Both are Class-5 Content statements (rank 4, same coordinate) under Curricular Goal CG-3, but sit under different competencies: 'Uses patterns to decode messages involving alphabet and numerals' under C-3.4 (identifying/describing/extending patterns) and 'Creating and extending tiling and tessellation patterns' under C-3.1 (attributes of 2D/3D shapes). Their Learning Components ('use patterns to decode messages involving numerals/the alphabet' vs 'create/extend tiling and tessellation patterns') show genuine shared pattern-rule reasoning applied in two distinct media — symbolic alphanumeric codes versus geometric plane-filling arrangements — so they are complementary reinforcing applications rather than one deepening the other. With equal rank and no evidence that either proficiency conditions success in the other (decoding coded messages does not presuppose tessellation construction, or vice versa), symmetric relatesTo fits and buildsTowards is unsupported. Evidence limits: only shared token 'patterns' (jaccard ~0.15) links the texts, source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), and ancestor competencies/goal lack developmental coordinates, so the coherence judgment rests on the bounded statement and LC text alone.
